claims.text: Progressive plastic deformation under sustained loading in FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy multilayers is governed by the evolution of interfacial structure.
The starting multilayers have sharp, chemically distinct interfaces with high crystallographic coherence.
Rapid thermal annealing can create narrow graded interfacial zones without destroying the nanoscale layering.
Adjusting substrate temperature and deposition rate can produce controlled interface misfit and reduced crystallographic coherence.
Graded compositional zones reduce local lattice-distortion gradients at FCC/BCC interfaces.
Reducing lattice distortion facilitates dislocation motion or transmission.
Engineered interface misfit induces incipient amorphous or highly disordered interfacial zones.
The combination of graded interfacial chemistry and tailored crystallographic misfit causes localized interfacial softening.
Graded chemistry and tailored misfit ease dislocation transmission across interfaces.
Localized amorphization at interfaces contributes to softening.
Interfacial softening, enhanced dislocation transmission, and localized amorphization gradually accommodate plastic deformation during sustained loading.
At 450–550°C, diffusion is appreciable in the proposed multilayers.
The nanoscale multilayer architecture remains intact during creep testing at 450–550°C.
Engineered graded and misfit-tailored interfaces will produce increased localized dislocation activity relative to sharp-interface controls.
Engineered interfaces will have a higher density of incipient amorphous or disordered regions than sharp-interface controls.
Engineered graded and misfit-tailored interfaces will reduce creep resistance relative to as-deposited sharp-interface controls.
Sharp-interface controls will retain higher creep resistance and undergo less progressive plastic deformation.
The proposed behavior occurs only when interdiffusion is moderate enough to preserve the multilayer architecture.
Excessive interdiffusion or loss of nanoscale layering lies outside the hypothesis regime.
TEM, atom-probe tomography, diffraction, and nanoindentation creep measurements can respectively assess interfacial disorder, chemical gradients, coherence or strain, and creep response.

contradictions.description: Loss of multilayer architecture is defined as outside the hypothesis regime, but uncontrolled architectural compromise is also treated as falsification. An out-of-regime or confounded specimen cannot by itself decisively falsify the proposed in-regime mechanism.
